title: fix: avoid compaction from superseded history
body:
Closes #150579

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: stale-usage preflight triggers unnecessary compaction after a session has already compacted but retains a large display history.

## User Impact

User impact: healthy compacted sessions proceed without another budget compaction. Genuinely oversized active contexts still trigger compaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing asynchronous canonical model-context reader for the no-usage estimate, preserving the summary, retained tail, tool pairs, and newer messages while excluding superseded history. Headerless legacy projections retain their existing fallback.

The contributor's implementation and commits are preserved. Removed an unused re-export left by an earlier revision. Strengthened the real-Gateway regression to assert that no second compaction entry is persisted: one model request alone was not sufficient, because the baseline performed an unnecessary compaction without an extra provider request.

The new reader also recognizes an explicitly selected incognito database, not only an incognito-shaped session key. Such databases stay with their existing process-local owner instead of being reopened as empty worker-local databases.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes. Thanks to @goutamadwant for the fix and @BillBOT33 for the report.

## Evidence

Secretless Docker, built runtimes, synthetic persisted sessions, explicit isolated profiles, loopback mock Anthropic transport, and real authenticated Gateway `agent` turns. Baseline: current main `3f263ba918c56e5c227261cb67be910e64bef74d`.

Each healthy fixture retained 650,000 characters of superseded history behind a compaction boundary, with a short summary/tail and stale usage. The model window was 100,000 tokens; the blocking threshold was 80,000.

| Scenario | Transcript estimate | Estimate including new prompt | Observed behavior |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Main, healthy compacted context | 162,505 | 162,512 | Budget compaction triggered and persisted a second compaction entry |
| Candidate, identical context | 11 | 18 | No compaction triggered; one original boundary remained; reply completed and persisted |
| Candidate, genuinely large active context | 93,758 | 93,765 | Budget compaction triggered and completed; reply completed |

The healthy candidate's single provider request included the summary, active tail, and new prompt, but not the superseded marker. Memory flushing was disabled in this proof; it exercises the compaction path, not the reporter's complete hook/draining sequence.

- SQLite-backed regression: failed on main because compaction was called; candidate file passed all 9 tests (45.80 s command wall time, 43.88 s Vitest duration). The first hosted run also passed all 9 tests in 24.97 s Vitest time (26.90 s command wall time).
- Strengthened real-Gateway regression: failed on main with two persisted compaction entries instead of one; passed on the candidate (61.85 s command wall time, 34.92 s test time). The isolated driver used the committed scenario/assertions with explicit profiles and retained diagnostics. Gateway startup and a real provider round trip account for the runtime; the cheaper SQLite tests separately cover the estimate boundary.
- Large-active-context Gateway control passed (47.42 s command wall time).
- The first hosted run exposed a related incognito admission regression ([failing case](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36847619709/job/110321946926)). A new physical-incognito row in the existing context-reader matrix failed with the same read-fence error before the owner correction. Afterward, all 38 context-reader tests and all 222 reply-agent tests passed, including that admission case (406.24 s combined command wall time; 72.85 s and 257.60 s Vitest durations). The added row itself took 76 ms.
- Rebuilt after the incognito correction. Two real Gateway turns in the supported incognito session namespace completed with zero provider-usage anchors; the second request retained the first turn, and no incognito SQLite file was created (22.26 s command wall time). An initial smoke setup pointing the global session store directly at the incognito sentinel was rejected before execution; the successful smoke uses the normal incognito route.
- Both isolated runtime builds passed. Initial E2E wrapper attempts redundantly rebuilt the runtime; those setup attempts were stopped, then the documented prebuilt-runtime mode was used.
- `git diff --check` passed.

### Compatibility

Read-only selection change: no SQLite schema, serialized row, writer, migration, or retention changes. The persisted-session fixtures use the existing format. This does not require a data-model migration. The legacy read fallback remains intact.

Disclosure: AI assisted with implementation review and validation.
